:::{#hero-heading}

Thanks for stopping by!

I’m Richard Liu, a Ph.D. trainee at NYU Grossman School of Medicine, where I’m supervised by [Dr. Ivan Diaz](https://idiaz.xyz/). I also collaborate with other researchers including [Dr. Wenbo Wu](https://www.wenbowu.me/), [Dr. Michele Santacatterina](https://michelesantacatterina.github.io/), and [Dr. Alex Luedtke](https://alexluedtke.com/).

I’m interested in developing and applying modern statistical methods to questions in public health and medicine. My research focuses on causal machine learning, semiparametric theory, mediation analysis, and causal inference with time-varying treatments and outcomes. I’ve also worked on projects involving transportability, causal fairness, and applications of large language models (LLMs) to causal inference.

Outside of research, I enjoy cooking, exercising, including fitness training and archery, and playing card and video games.

Please feel free to reach out if you’re interested in collaborating!

## Education

- PhD, NYU Grossman School of Medicine, Expected 2027

## Experience

- Ph.D. Statistics Intern, Eli Lilly and Company, 05/2026-08/2026
